doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: Staff jobs at NBC and the first Carson band
summary: Staff work meant staying home with good pay; he describes the live-show era and the first Carson band under Skitch.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: When the big band era kind of faded out, a lot of the musicians found a home —

Oh yes, it was the best job. You don’t have to travel anymore. You stayed home and the money was good, and you were treated nicely, and if you worked — this was before tapes, so you had to be there live, you know the live shows. And then Carson came along. And Skitch again went right in with that. And he was the band leader on the first Carson show. And that was a wonderful band, it was great band. Doc Severinsen of course was there, all of — Tommy Newsom as a matter of fact was in that band. Hymie Shertzer from Benny Goodman. Clark Terry, Snooky Young, all giants, you know, musical giants. And we saw each other more than we saw our kids, our families, because these were live shows, they were live. And we made them, they were put together with spit and chewing gum, we just floated through. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
